claude.sample_unit: trials (10 per custom GPT per model, plus 10 standard-prompt trials)

links.outcome: Reproducibility of extraction across 10 repeated runs; structured custom prompts vs standard prompts
links.effect: Both models had high reproducibility (at least 8/10 outputs consistent or partially consistent). Custom GPT extracted exactly 2 benefits per trial (SD 0.0); standard prompts averaged 5.3 (SD 1.8, range 3-8).
links.quote: Both models demonstrated high reproducibility, with at least 8 out of 10 outputs from each GPT rated as “consistent” or “partially consistent” ( Table 3 ).

links.outcome: Accuracy difference between GPT-4 and GPT-4o on research objectives extraction
links.effect: GPT-4 achieved 30% accuracy on research objectives and background vs 80% for GPT-4o, showing model version changes alter performance; other elements 100% in both.
links.quote: In contrast, GPT-4 achieved only 30% extraction accuracy for “research objectives and background” but demonstrated 100% extraction accuracy for the other two elements ( Table 2 ).

links.outcome: Reference standard quality and rater independence in evaluating output accuracy
links.effect: Evaluation used one unblinded evaluator with no inter-rater agreement and no verified gold standard, so subjective bias may have affected results.
links.quote: The evaluation was conducted by a single researcher, and inter-rater agreement was not assessed.

links.outcome: Effect of document format on extraction output stability
links.effect: ChatGPT struggled with complex-structure or image-text PDFs; converting to Word and standardizing headings significantly improved output stability (qualitative, no numbers).
links.quote: From a technical perspective, we observed that ChatGPT struggled with PDF files that had complex structures or contained text stored as images.

unlisted_practices: Structured, section-specific custom prompts to improve extraction accuracy and consistency
Standardizing input document format (Word, standardized headings) before LLM processing

openai.sample_unit: AI-generated output trials from one mock protocol/ICF

links.effect: GPT-4o: 80% for objectives/background and 100% for design and risks/benefits; GPT-4: 30% for objectives/background and 100% for other two elements.
links.quote: GPT-4o achieved 80% extraction accuracy for the “research objectives and background” element, and 100% extraction accuracy for both “research design” and “participant-related risks and benefits” ( Table 1 ).

links.effect: Both GPT-4o and GPT-4 had high reproducibility: at least 8/10 outputs from each GPT were consistent or partially consistent.
links.quote: Both models demonstrated high reproducibility, with at least 8 out of 10 outputs from each GPT rated as “consistent” or “partially consistent” ( Table 3 ).

links.effect: GPTs-3 extracted 2.0 benefits (SD 0.0; min/max 2/2); standard prompts 5.3 (SD 1.8; min 3, max 8).
links.quote: In contrast, outputs generated using standard prompts showed greater variability in both the number and type of extracted participant-related benefits, with categories and counts differing significantly across trials ( Tables 4 and 5 ).

links.effect: Complex PDFs or image-stored text made ChatGPT struggle; Word conversion and standardized headings significantly improved output stability; no quantitative values reported.
links.quote: From a technical perspective, we observed that ChatGPT struggled with PDF files that had complex structures or contained text stored as images.

links.outcome: extraction accuracy and reproducibility across trials
links.effect: Customized prompts extracted 2.0 (SD 0.0) benefits consistently across 10 trials, whereas standard prompts averaged 5.3 (SD 1.8, range 3-8) with high category variability across trials.
links.quote: GPTs with customized prompts produced more accurate and consistent outputs than standard prompts.
